1. Verify current bill arithmetic: confirm meter reads imply 1,489 kWh (87,669 − 86,180), line items sum to $257.70 ($18.38 + $39.18 + $200.14), and the total change versus last month is +$49.03 ($257.70 − $208.67).

2. Map both billing periods to the OpenEI tariff: last month (2025-12-12 to 2026-01-09) and current (2026-01-09 to 2026-02-12) both fall under the same tariff (fixed $18.38; first-tier variable $0.0263125 + $0.13441 = $0.1607225/kWh for ≤2,000 kWh), so price_usd = 0 unless a rate difference is found.

3. Compute days_usd: because the fixed charge is monthly rather than per-day and no daily line items exist, the longer 34-day vs 28-day period contributes $0; set days_usd = 0.

4. Estimate weather_usd: compare NOAA degree days (last month HDD 882 / CDD 0 vs current HDD 1,502 / CDD 0), fit a weather-to-kWh relationship from the bill history, convert the weather-driven kWh difference to dollars at the effective variable rate.

5. Compute usage_usd: start with the total usage increase (1,489 − 1,184 = 305 kWh), subtract weather-attributable kWh, value the remaining household-driven kWh at the effective rate, then set usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly +$49.03.

6. Check for a billing error: compare the tariff-modeled total to the stated $257.70 and confirm billed kWh match meter reads; if the discrepancy exceeds rounding, set billing_error_suspected = true with billing_error_usd equal to the mismatch, otherwise false and null.

7. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
